items.canonical_answer: A small preliminary trial of research procedures before the main enquiry, used to identify and correct practical problems.
marking_guidance: Meaning: a small preliminary trial used to identify and correct procedure problems before the main enquiry; one indicative definition mark.

items.prompt: Describe how an invented learner could pilot a questionnaire about journeys to a water point before the main enquiry.
items.canonical_answer: Try the draft with a few relevant volunteers, observe whether they understand each question, record confusing wording and revise it. Try the revision to check whether the difficulty has been reduced before collecting the main data.
marking_guidance: Sequence: trial the draft, observe and record difficulties, revise, and re-test; these are the four procedural elements of this original four-mark practice question.
Application: carry out these steps with the stated water-journey questionnaire and relevant volunteers, rather than reciting only the term.
This is an original indicative practice rubric, not a universal official mark-per-bullet rule.
items.provenance: Original Codex structural example; final subject is designated for Codex authorship and independent Claude Code review.

items.prompt: Suggest a practical repair after four of six pilot participants ask what “a long water journey” means. Explain why the repair helps the enquiry.
items.canonical_answer: Ask for the number of minutes for a return journey and specify that waiting time is included. A common measure removes the ambiguous word long and makes the responses more comparable. Check the revised instruction in a further trial.
marking_guidance: Context: four of six pilot participants do not understand long journey; change the actual wording.

Reason: minutes for a return journey including waiting give a shared measurement rule; re-test comprehension. Three indicative practice marks for an actionable revision, clarity of measurement and reason.
This is an original indicative practice rubric, not a universal official mark-per-bullet rule.

items.prompt: Describe a pilot procedure for an invented water-journey questionnaire [3]. Suggest a response to this trial result: four of six volunteers do not understand “long journey” [3].
items.canonical_answer: Try the instrument with relevant volunteers, observe and record their difficulties, then revise and re-test it. Replace long journey with return-journey time in minutes including waiting; that gives participants a common rule. Record whether the revision is understood before the main collection. This is a procedural repair, not evidence about settlement-wide journey times.
marking_guidance: Method: try with relevant volunteers, observe/record the difficulty and revise/re-test; up to three indicative practice marks.
Evidence: use the recorded four-of-six ambiguity rather than inventing a different pilot finding.
Response: replace vague wording with return minutes including waiting and explain the common rule; up to three indicative marks.
This is an original indicative practice rubric, not a universal official mark-per-bullet rule.
